operations.name: Saw – Inner Member Blank
operations.setup_note: Clamp round stock against the length stop and cut the inner-member blank with allowance for facing both ends. Stock arrives unhardened, with its material grade pending confirmation.

operations.name: CNC Turn – First End
operations.setup_note: Grip the unmachined right-end flange region in bored soft jaws with the -X end exposed, then establish datum A. Rough the accessible OD and cavity before finishing the tapered cavity, journal B and bonding diameter in this chucking.

operations.name: CNC Turn – Second End
operations.setup_note: Reverse the inner member into nonmarking soft jaws on journal B, with datum A against an axial stop and the +X end exposed. Establish shoulder D and flange E, machine the right recess, and drill the central bore through the remaining web into the existing tapered cavity.

operations.name: VMC – Three-Hole Pattern
operations.setup_note: Hold the inner member in a split pot fixture on journal B, pick up datum A as the axial reference, and present the -X direction to the spindle. Provide tool and breakout clearance for the complete pattern, using released basic coordinates rather than assumed equal spacing.

operations.name: Outer Sleeve – Manufacture to Print
operations.setup_note: Procure the standard Item 2 outer sleeve manufactured to its released component drawing, including finished OD and end faces. Its position relative to D–E is established during bonded assembly, not during independent sleeve manufacture.

operations.name: Bench – Deburr and Clean
operations.setup_note: Present the machined inner member and supplied outer sleeve as a component kit for one fast edge-break and degreasing pass. Remove hole-entry and breakout burrs, observing the 0.5 mm maximum general edge break without altering the specified journal chamfer.

operations.name: Bond Preparation – Metal Components
operations.setup_note: Rack the clean metal components on a dedicated preparation fixture, protecting finished locating surfaces while preparing only the rubber-contact surfaces and applying the qualified bonding system. The vendor determines rack capacity; the 100-piece order is not assumed to fit one load.

operations.name: Bonded Insert Moulding and Vulcanization
operations.setup_note: Locate the prepared inner member from D and E in the bonding mould and positively locate the outer sleeve to maintain its specified position during rubber moulding and cure. Mould the body and rate-dependent relief, vulcanize, trim flash in the retained mould nest, and unload in vendor-defined production lots rather than one 100-piece furnace batch.

operations.name: Final Shop-Floor Gauge and Functional Gate
operations.setup_note: After cure stabilization, load finished assemblies into the dedicated gauge/test fixture using the separate A–B and D–E reference frames. Check critical fits, pattern position and sleeve alignment under SPC, with sampled rubber spring-rate and bond-function checks performed in the in-house test lab to TS-833410.

assumptions.text: This is a bonded multi-component assembly, not a monolithic turned bushing. The inner metal member is machined in-house, the standard outer sleeve is sourced manufactured-to-print, and the elastomer is moulded and bonded by a qualified outside supplier.

The single stock object represents only the inner-member blank. Its provisional Ø205 × 148.2 mm dimensions conservatively use the supplied assembly envelope plus allowances; the separate outer sleeve and elastomer are purchased inputs not representable as additional stock objects.

Metal components are provisionally unhardened and medium-machinability, with unknown HRC. Rubber vulcanization is polymer curing, not a metal-hardening operation, so it does not trigger hardened machinability.

The standard outer-sleeve configuration is used. Its inside diameter is not inferred from flange F10: the extracted Ø188 flange dimension does not establish the independent sleeve ID or wall thickness.
F03 is provisionally assigned to the exposed moulded elastomer body, while F12 is a mould-generated relief void. Neither is routed as an additional metal OD step or a lathe groove.

F07 uses the graph's R65.8 radius interpretation. The extracted assumption describing a Ø68.8/62.8 entrance and a 6° included taper is not adopted; the actual taper and controlled depth require release.

F02 connects the tapered cavity and right recess through the remaining inner-member web. The larger cavities are machined first; peck drilling is retained provisionally because the effective small-bore length is unresolved.

F04 is machined in the inner metal member from -X in one dedicated VMC fixture. Pilot drilling precedes full-size drilling; the metal penetration is provisionally treated as a shallow flange passage, with no assumed equal angular spacing or unsupported 3 mm counterbore depth.

Exactly two CNC lathe setups make the inner member. Separate rough and finish entries for Ø154, Ø142 and Ø188 are diameter-specific portions of consolidated profile cycles, not repeated full-stock removal or separate chuckings.

Turning-template center support is omitted for the short blank; spotting for bore opening remains. Metal grooving and threading are omitted because none is defined, and part-off is omitted because the blank is already saw-cut. Both axial ends and the datum shoulder are explicitly faced.

Milling-template stock cutting is shared with operation 1, and rotational datum facing and concentric recess machining are performed on the lathe. Profile, pocket and slot milling, reaming and tapping are omitted because the graph defines no corresponding prismatic contours, precision-fit holes or threads.

Large cavity opening uses spot/pilot drilling followed by boring rather than drilling to full cavity diameter. Hole-making reaming, tapping and honing are omitted because no such finish or thread is specified; hole deburring is consolidated into the single bench pass.

The retrieved thermoplastic injection-moulding and fibre-composite sequences do not apply literally to this elastomer-to-metal assembly. Thermoplastic drying, packing/cooling rules, annealing, ply cutting, lay-up, vacuum bagging, autoclave processing, laminate drilling, NDT and protective painting are omitted; moulding, polymer cure, demoulding and flash trimming are adapted to the qualified rubber process.

Bond-contact surfaces receive provisional abrasive preparation and a qualified primer/adhesive system, subject to the governing process specification. No decorative or corrosion-protection coating, metal heat treatment or grinding is added without an explicit requirement.

The external moulding supplier retains each assembly in its mould nest through cure and flash trimming before unloading. There is one production bench deburr/clean gate; tooling manufacture, mould trials and test-fixture manufacture are separately quoted one-time activities.

All template inspection steps are consolidated into one final shop-floor gate, without intermediate gates or CMM layout. The second manual_inspect entry represents sampled instrumented rubber functional checks because the controlled vocabulary has no rubber spring-rate test type; a provisional 1-in-50 sampling rate gives two samples for this order, subject to TS-833410.
